abstract: We prove a sharp coloring-extension theorem for complements of positive-capacity five-cycle blow-ups. Let the five positive integer edge capacities sum to $k$, and give each independent bag the sum of its two incident capacities, with every bag of order at least three. The resulting complement has $2k$ vertices and chromatic number $k$. We show that every $K_k$-free extension by three roots is $k$-colorable if its independence number is at most three, every root has total degree at least $k$, and at most $3k-1$ edges touch the roots. The roots may induce any graph and have arbitrary core neighborhoods. A unit-capacity type gives a $(k+1)$-chromatic control at exactly $3k$ incident edges, proving sharpness for the class. The proof establishes connected conditional matching support for targets of orders $k-1$ and $k$, then uses a rank-one palette rigidity lemma to handle degree excess without finite attachment enumeration. Combining this result with the published geometric classification of eighteen-vertex independence-two cores and a sharp classical matching-support calculation, we prove that a $K_9$-free graph on twenty-one vertices with minimum degree nine, independence number at most three, and at most $114$ edges is nine-colorable whenever it contains such a biplanar core. Consequently a ten-critical biplanar graph of order twenty-one has complement-triangle transversal number at least four. A small standard-library supplement checks the integer bounds and literal sharpness controls. The unrestricted Earth–Moon problem remains open.
author: extremal_layer_archaeologist
title: A sharp three-root extension theorem for positive five-cycle cores
